space.name: Public Organization Space
space.description: Organizations wielding delegated public authority under law: ministries, councils, delivery and research bodies, task groups, arm's-length agencies, state-owned enterprises, municipalities, and public-private hybrids.

universe.description: Public organizations wielding delegated public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under constitutional, statutory, customary, dynastic, party, military, colonial, feudal, or treaty-based arrangements.
excludes: informal groups without a constituting order

meta.description: Four comparative representation systems for comparing public organizations across polities and periods: ontological, functional, purpose-driven, and model-derived.

systems.name: ontological
systems.title: Ontological Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies are: their legal standing, institutional kind, composition, resources, permanence, and spatial definition. Derived by ontological analysis - enumerating the entities, kinds, and modes of existence the domain contains. Use it to compare bodies as entities before asking what they do or how they relate.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the organization decomposition and agency-form comparison
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, dynastic, party, military, colonial, feudal, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies are: existence, kind, composition, and permanence.

groups.name: Existence & Standing
groups.description: What the body is as a legal or institutional entity.

groups.name: Composition & Maintenance
groups.description: How the body is staffed and how its post-holders are sustained.

groups.name: Resources & Financing
groups.description: The material resources the body commands and how its operation is financed.

groups.name: Authority & Continuity
groups.description: The basis of its authority and how permanently it is constituted.

groups.name: Jurisdiction & Reach
groups.description: The territory, persons, or activities its authority runs over.

characteristic_element_set.name: Institutional Standing
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body holds legal personality, is a dependent public body, or is an office without personhood.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code independent where it owns property and litigates in its own name; dependent where it is a distinct public body lacking full personhood; office where the holder, not the body, holds the legal position.

characteristic_element_set.name: Organizational Form
characteristic_element_set.description: The recognized kind of public body or governing institution.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by constituting order and institutional function jointly. Use feudal lordship for a lordship exercising public or governing authority through a feudal tenure relationship; a private landholding alone is insufficient. Hybrids take public-private hybrid only under mixed control. Bodies chartered by more than one polity take supranational body.

characteristic_element_set.name: Recruitment Mode
characteristic_element_set.description: The dominant mode by which members or post-holders are installed.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the mode filling the majority of the deciding membership or relevant posts. Use mixed where no mode predominates. Appointment by institutional authority describes the appointing mechanism; record the appointing actor separately where relevant.

characteristic_element_set.name: Office Maintenance
characteristic_element_set.description: How the post-holder is materially sustained.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant material basis of the office. Use fief / feudal tenure where maintenance derives from tenure carrying feudal obligations; distinguish this from simple ownership or rental income.

characteristic_element_set.name: Resource Base
characteristic_element_set.description: The largest class of resources the body commands.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the dominant resource commanded by the body; bodies without holdings take none. Use fief / feudal domain only where land or rights are held within a feudal tenure relationship.

characteristic_element_set.name: Financing Mode
characteristic_element_set.description: The revenue base financing the body's operation.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the largest revenue share over the body's operating period. Feudal dues are obligations attached to feudal tenure; ordinary land rents are coded as benefice / land revenue.

characteristic_element_set.name: Authority Basis
characteristic_element_set.description: The basis on which the body's authority rests.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal basis supporting the body's authority, not merely its source of income. Where authority rests on several inseparable bases, use mixed. Feudal tenure / vassalic obligation applies where authority and duties derive from a feudal relationship.

characteristic_element_set.name: Permanence
characteristic_element_set.description: How permanently the body is constituted.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Read the constituting order: a dissolution clause gives task-bound; a fixed end date gives fixed-term; a renewal term gives renewable mandate; otherwise permanent.

characteristic_element_set.name: Jurisdictional Extent
characteristic_element_set.description: The scale at which the body's authority runs.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the polity that constitutes it and the reach of its remit, not solely by where it operates.

characteristic_element_set.name: Territorial Basis
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether authority runs over people, land, function, or beyond territory.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code personal where the remit follows persons or status; territorial where it follows bounded land; functional where it follows an activity or regulated domain.

characteristic_element_set.name: Mandate Scope
characteristic_element_set.description: How wide the constituting remit runs.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Count the domains named in the constituting order, not those grown by practice.

systems.name: functional
systems.title: Functional Set
systems.description: Profiles what public bodies do: the task families they perform, coded by exercised activity rather than charter rhetoric. Derived by functional analysis - enumerating the functions and activities of the domain. Use it to compare workloads and task portfolios across bodies with different legal forms.
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the function taxonomy and agency mandates
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, dynastic, party, military, colonial, feudal, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Compare what bodies do: task families by exercised activity.

groups.name: Provision & Service
groups.description: Delivering services, protection, or provision to end users.

groups.name: Regulation & Enforcement
groups.description: Forming binding rules and compelling compliance.

groups.name: Extraction & Commerce
groups.description: Drawing resources from, or trading with, the governed.

groups.name: Knowledge & Symbol
groups.description: Producing knowledge, records, and symbolic or ideological output.

groups.name: Force & Representation
groups.description: Raising organized force and aggregating constituencies.

groups.name: Coordination & Emergency
groups.description: Coordinating other bodies and holding extraordinary powers.

characteristic_element_set.name: Service & Provision
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body delivers services, protection, or provision to end users.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant provision; commissioned where it funds or compels others to deliver; none for bodies that only rule or extract.

characteristic_element_set.name: Regulation
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body forms binding rules, licenses, or authoritative counsel.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code rule-making where it issues binding rules in its own right; licensing where its only binding act is granting or refusing permissions; advisory where it only counsels; none otherwise.

characteristic_element_set.name: Enforcement
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body compels compliance.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the highest exercised in its operating period; inspection without sanction stays inspection.

characteristic_element_set.name: Adjudication
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body decides individual cases with binding effect.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code binding only where decisions are enforceable without further approval.

characteristic_element_set.name: Resource Extraction
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body draws resources from the population or governed entities.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant mode by which it draws resources; feudal dues apply to obligations attached to feudal tenure; bodies that only spend take none.

characteristic_element_set.name: Knowledge and Record
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body produces knowledge, records, or evidence.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant knowledge and record function; distinguish internal production from commissioned work and routine record-keeping.

characteristic_element_set.name: Ideological and Symbolic Administration
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body performs ideological propagation, public symbolism, or institutional legitimation as an administrative function.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code a function only where it is an identifiable organizational activity; classify other activities by their substantive function. Do not infer this function merely from an organization's historical association or symbols.

characteristic_element_set.name: Military Mobilization
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body raises, commands, or supplies organized force.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant military function; bodies with no force function take none.

characteristic_element_set.name: Representation
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body aggregates estates, communities, or constituencies.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code where the body's dominant function is to voice or aggregate constituencies or recognized social bodies.

characteristic_element_set.name: Coordination & Oversight
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body coordinates or supervises other bodies.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code lead coordinator where it convenes and sets the agenda of a standing coordination arrangement; supervisory only with a formal oversight mandate over named bodies.

characteristic_element_set.name: Commercial Operation
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body operates commercially or by trading monopoly.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the pricing rule and purpose of its trading activity; bodies with no trading activity take none.

characteristic_element_set.name: Emergency Powers
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether the body holds extraordinary powers.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code standing where powers are exercisable without fresh authorization.

systems.name: purpose-driven
systems.title: Purpose-Driven Set
systems.description: Profiles what decision-makers need to know: answerability, changeability, rationalization, centralization, embeddedness, fidelity of performance signals, and risk. Derived by purpose-driven analysis - starting from the questions, decisions, and analytical tasks the comparison must support, then selecting the elements that answer them. Use it when a decision, not a description, is the output.
systems.frame_basis: Purpose-driven analysis from canonical comparison questions
systems.provenance: authored for this atlas from the evaluation and governance questions
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under any basis of authority - constitutional, statutory, customary, dynastic, party, military, colonial, feudal, or treaty.
systems.purpose: Answer decisions: answerability, changeability, rationalization, centralization, embeddedness, risk.

groups.name: Answerability
groups.description: Whether and how the body is answerable and observable.

groups.name: Adaptability & Structure
groups.description: How the body can be changed and how authority is distributed.

groups.name: Administrative Model
groups.description: The dominant basis of authority and administration.

groups.name: Mandate Specification
groups.description: How precisely the mandate defines success.

groups.name: Exposure & Loss
groups.description: Exposure to capture and who bears residual loss.

characteristic_element_set.name: Accountability Depth
characteristic_element_set.description: Whether answerability carries consequences.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code full where an accountability cycle can trigger and has credible capacity to trigger leadership, financial, legal, or operational consequences; reporting alone is reporting only.

characteristic_element_set.name: Changeability
characteristic_element_set.description: How the body can be reorganized or abolished.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the instrument or force needed for abolition or fundamental reorganization in the body's institutional order.

characteristic_element_set.name: Rationalization Degree
characteristic_element_set.description: The dominant basis of organizational authority and administration, distinguishing rule-bound office from personal, patrimonial, charismatic, and customary arrangements.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code rational-legal bureaucracy where offices are rule-defined and administration is impersonal and career-based; patrimonial where offices are personal extensions of a ruler's household; feudal where authority and obligations are organized through feudal tenure and personal bonds; use mixed where no form dominates.

characteristic_element_set.name: Centralization
characteristic_element_set.description: How decision-making authority is distributed across levels and units.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the location of effective decision rights, distinguishing local execution under central control from delegated or autonomous local authority.

characteristic_element_set.name: Loss Bearer
characteristic_element_set.description: Who bears the financial or material residual loss.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by who absorbs deficits or losses in practice, not merely who is formally liable.

characteristic_element_set.name: Performance Visibility
characteristic_element_set.description: How observable the body's performance is to outsiders.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the strongest regular mechanism available to external observers; distinguish published performance measures from records or inspection.

characteristic_element_set.name: Mandate Clarity
characteristic_element_set.description: How precisely the mandate states what success looks like.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code from the constituting order and binding directives, not from observed performance.

characteristic_element_set.name: Capture Exposure
characteristic_element_set.description: Exposure to capture by concentrated interests or insiders.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Assess safeguards, concentration of beneficiaries or regulated parties, transparency, appointment arrangements, and conflicts of interest. Do not infer low exposure from tenure protection alone.

characteristic_element_set.name: Patron-Client Position
characteristic_element_set.description: The body's position within patronage, faction, or personal-dependence networks.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code central patron where the body dispenses offices or resources through a dependent network; code client where its own position depends on another patron; distinguish evidence of autonomy from lack of evidence.

systems.name: model-derived
systems.title: Model-Derived Set
systems.description: Derives characteristics from an overarching model of public organization as an institutional operating system: constitution, mandate, authority, governance, organization, operations, resources and capabilities, accountability and control, and institutional ecology. Each submodel contributes elements to a composite profile. Formal arrangements and observed practice should be distinguished where they differ.
systems.frame_basis: Composite-model approach: Public Organization Model in nine submodels
systems.provenance: revised model decomposition for this atlas; enriched to represent authority relationships, internal organization, operating arrangements, capabilities, control, and institutional ecology
systems.universe: Bodies exercising or asserting public authority over a population or territory, in any polity and any period, under constitutional, statutory, customary, dynastic, party, military, colonial, feudal, or treaty-based arrangements.
systems.purpose: Reconstruct how the organization is constituted, authorized, governed, organized, operated, resourced, controlled, and embedded in a wider institutional system.

submodels.name: Constitution
submodels.question: How does the organization come into existence?

submodels.name: Mandate
submodels.question: What is the organization authorized and expected to accomplish?

submodels.name: Authority
submodels.question: From whom does its authority derive, and to whom is it answerable?

submodels.name: Governance
submodels.question: How is the organization directed and how are decisions made?

submodels.name: Organization
submodels.question: How is work and authority divided and coordinated internally?

submodels.name: Operations
submodels.question: How does the organization turn its mandate into action and results?

submodels.name: Resources and Capabilities
submodels.question: What enables the organization to operate?

submodels.name: Accountability and Control
submodels.question: How are conduct, expenditure, and results monitored and corrected?

submodels.name: Institutional Ecology
submodels.question: How does the organization interact with its surrounding institutional environment?

representation_rules.formal_and_observed: Where materially different, record formal arrangements and observed practice separately, each with evidence and a reference period.
representation_rules.cardinality: Use single values for exclusive characteristics, multiple values for coexisting functions or mechanisms, quantitative values for measurable shares, and relationship records for interorganizational relations.
representation_rules.temporal_validity: Record valid_from and valid_to for characteristics and relationships that change over time.
representation_rules.evidence: Each coded observation should retain source, date, confidence, and a concise rationale where available.

relationship_schema.description: Represent authority and institutional ecology relationships explicitly rather than collapsing them into a single categorical field.

characteristic_element_set.name: Constituting Instrument
characteristic_element_set.description: The instrument or institutional order through which the organization is established.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Cite the constituting instrument or institutional evidence. Use multiple where the organization rests on several instruments.

characteristic_element_set.name: Institutional Standing
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's institutional or legal status.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the legal or historically evidenced institutional status; do not infer legal personality from operational independence.

characteristic_element_set.name: Institutional Origin
characteristic_element_set.description: The process through which the organization was established.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the event or process that directly produced the organization in its present institutional form.

characteristic_element_set.name: Permanence
characteristic_element_set.description: The intended duration of the organization.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Use the constituting order and subsequent valid amendments; distinguish a permanent body from a fixed-term mandate.

characteristic_element_set.name: Mandate Scope
characteristic_element_set.description: The breadth of the organization's assigned responsibilities.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the breadth of the formal mandate, not every activity later assumed in practice.

characteristic_element_set.name: Mandate Orientation
characteristic_element_set.description: The principal kind of result the organization is expected to produce.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the orientation emphasized by the mandate; use mixed where multiple orientations are materially coequal.

characteristic_element_set.name: Jurisdictional Extent
characteristic_element_set.description: The geographic or jurisdictional reach of its authority.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the formal jurisdiction and reach, not merely the physical location of headquarters.

characteristic_element_set.name: Target Population
characteristic_element_set.description: The population or entities toward which the mandate is directed.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the intended subjects, clients, beneficiaries, or regulated entities named in the mandate.

characteristic_element_set.name: Mandate Precision
characteristic_element_set.description: How explicitly the mandate defines expected results.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the formal degree of specification, not whether the organization actually meets the mandate.

characteristic_element_set.name: Reserved Powers
characteristic_element_set.description: Powers expressly retained by the principal or another authority rather than assigned to the organization.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Record the reserved powers and the authority retaining them, citing the relevant instrument.

characteristic_element_set.name: Political Principal
characteristic_element_set.description: The authority to which the organization's leadership is ultimately answerable.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the authority with effective appointment, direction, or dismissal powers; if these are divided, use multiple principals and record each relationship separately. A feudal overlord / suzerain applies only where the organization participates in a feudal authority relationship.

characteristic_element_set.name: Appointment Authority
characteristic_element_set.description: The actor empowered to appoint the organization's leadership.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the formal appointing actor or mechanism; use multiple where appointments are shared or differ by office.

characteristic_element_set.name: Direction Authority
characteristic_element_set.description: The actor authorized to issue binding instructions to the organization.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the actor with formal or evidenced authority to issue binding instructions; distinguish influence from direction authority.

characteristic_element_set.name: Dismissal Authority
characteristic_element_set.description: The actor empowered to remove the organization's leadership.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the actor or mechanism with authority to remove or replace leadership; distinguish formal power from practical influence.

characteristic_element_set.name: Delegation Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: How authority is transferred to the organization.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal mechanism by which authority is conferred; feudal grant / investiture applies where authority and tenure are linked through a feudal relationship.

characteristic_element_set.name: Operational Autonomy
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's discretion in executing its mandate.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code observed discretion in routine operations separately from formal autonomy where the two differ.

characteristic_element_set.name: Governing Structure
characteristic_element_set.description: The arrangement responsible for organizational direction.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the arrangement that can settle direction and overrule the chief executive; record formal and observed arrangements separately where needed.

characteristic_element_set.name: Decision Procedure
characteristic_element_set.description: How contested authoritative decisions are reached.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Test with a contested decision and identify the procedure that settles it; distinguish the procedure from the body's governing structure.

characteristic_element_set.name: Decision Rights
characteristic_element_set.description: How decision authority is distributed across leadership and internal units.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the observed distribution of consequential decision rights, not merely the organization chart.

characteristic_element_set.name: Leadership Tenure
characteristic_element_set.description: The formal basis and duration of leadership tenure.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal tenure rule for the chief leadership role; use mixed where leadership offices differ materially.

characteristic_element_set.name: Conflict Resolution
characteristic_element_set.description: How internal disagreements over authority or decisions are resolved.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the established mechanism used to resolve consequential internal disputes.

characteristic_element_set.name: Organizational Structure
characteristic_element_set.description: The dominant arrangement of internal units and reporting relationships.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant structure through which work and authority are divided; use feudal layered hierarchy only where authority is organized through layered lordship or tenure relationships.

characteristic_element_set.name: Functional Specialization
characteristic_element_set.description: How work is divided among organizational units.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal basis of work division across units.

characteristic_element_set.name: Territorial Deployment Structure
characteristic_element_set.description: How organizational units are distributed across jurisdiction.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the structural distribution of units or authority; distinguish formal unit structure from where work is actually performed.

characteristic_element_set.name: Internal Coordination
characteristic_element_set.description: How organizational units coordinate interdependent work.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant coordination mechanism; use personal allegiance / reciprocal obligation only where these are evidenced operating mechanisms rather than general social context.

characteristic_element_set.name: Shared Services Arrangement
characteristic_element_set.description: How common administrative capabilities are provided.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant arrangement for common functions such as finance, personnel, procurement, and information technology.

characteristic_element_set.name: Functions
characteristic_element_set.description: The task families performed by the organization in practice.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Use multiple values when several functions are materially present; identify the dominant function only where a summary value is required. Classify substantive activity rather than institutional identity or historical association.

characteristic_element_set.name: Operating Mode
characteristic_element_set.description: How the organization produces or secures intended results.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code who actually performs or secures the work; use feudal / intermediary rule where authority is exercised through subordinate lords or other intermediaries.

characteristic_element_set.name: Instruments of Action
characteristic_element_set.description: The principal means through which the organization attempts to achieve its objectives.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code instruments actually used, allowing multiple values where the organization relies on more than one materially important instrument.

characteristic_element_set.name: Operational Deployment
characteristic_element_set.description: Where and through what arrangement activities are performed.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Map where activities are performed and through what delivery arrangement, not merely where staff sit.

characteristic_element_set.name: Process Standardization
characteristic_element_set.description: How consistently work is performed across cases and units.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant actual operating procedure; distinguish written rules from practice where evidence permits.

characteristic_element_set.name: Service or Decision Interface
characteristic_element_set.description: How the organization interacts with the population, clients, or entities subject to its authority.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal interface through which subjects, beneficiaries, or regulated entities interact with the organization.

characteristic_element_set.name: Funding Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: The principal basis of financing.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code by the largest revenue share over the operating period; use mixed where no source predominates or sources are structurally inseparable.

characteristic_element_set.name: Personnel Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: How personnel are recruited, retained, and managed.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant installation and tenure mode. Feudal tenure / personal service obligation applies to offices or service obligations embedded in a feudal relationship, not merely to inherited employment.

characteristic_element_set.name: Resource Control
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's effective control over its resources.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the degree and form of effective control over funds and assets; tenure-bound domain control applies where rights are constrained by feudal obligations.

characteristic_element_set.name: Asset Base
characteristic_element_set.description: The principal physical and financial assets available to the organization.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the largest class of assets materially supporting the organization; distinguish a feudal domain from ordinary property ownership.

characteristic_element_set.name: Knowledge Capability
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's ability to produce, acquire, retain, and apply knowledge.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code demonstrated organizational capability rather than presumed expertise based on institutional status.

characteristic_element_set.name: Technical Capability
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's capacity to execute work through established methods, equipment, and technical systems.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the capabilities materially used in operations, not technology merely owned but unused.

characteristic_element_set.name: Accountability Line
characteristic_element_set.description: The actor or institution to which the organization must account.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code each material accountability relationship where possible; distinguish reporting recipients from authorities able to impose consequences.

characteristic_element_set.name: Reporting Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: The formal arrangement for reporting organizational activity.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the recurring reporting arrangement; customary or personal reporting requires evidence of a recognized obligation or practice.

characteristic_element_set.name: Financial Control
characteristic_element_set.description: The arrangement controlling expenditure and financial integrity.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the strongest regularly operating financial control mechanism supported by evidence; distinguish formal requirements from observed operation.

characteristic_element_set.name: Performance Control
characteristic_element_set.description: The arrangement used to assess organizational results and compliance.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the principal mechanism used to assess results; do not equate routine reporting with evaluation.

characteristic_element_set.name: Corrective Authority
characteristic_element_set.description: The actor empowered to require changes when deficiencies are identified.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the actor able to compel a corrective response, not merely recommend one.

characteristic_element_set.name: Sanction Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: The consequences available for misconduct or failure.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code sanctions institutionally available and evidenced; loss of tenure / fief applies where tenure rights can be withdrawn for breach of obligations.

characteristic_element_set.name: Interorganizational Position
characteristic_element_set.description: The organization's position relative to other bodies.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code position in relation to named organizations or authorities; where relations vary, store them as separate relationships rather than forcing one overall value.

characteristic_element_set.name: Coordination Regime
characteristic_element_set.description: How the organization coordinates with other institutions.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the dominant mechanism for coordinating interorganizational activity, not merely the presence of contacts.

characteristic_element_set.name: External Dependency
characteristic_element_set.description: Dependence on other organizations for essential capabilities or inputs.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Assess whether interruption of an external input, authority, provider, or relationship would materially impair core functions.

characteristic_element_set.name: Provision Relationship
characteristic_element_set.description: How services or outputs relate to external providers.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code who actually provides or enables the output; do not infer private provision solely from a public-private legal form.

characteristic_element_set.name: Institutional Adaptation
characteristic_element_set.description: How the organization can change its arrangements in response to its environment.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the observed capacity and mechanism for changing structure or operations, distinguishing formal constraints from practice.

characteristic_element_set.name: Institutional Succession
characteristic_element_set.description: How functions and assets are treated when the organization is reorganized or abolished.
characteristic_element_set.assignment_rule: Code the rule or observed process governing transfer of functions, assets, obligations, or tenure at dissolution or reorganization.
